title.narrative: Effective implementation of the National Action Plan for the elimination of the worst forms of child labour, including in plantation sectors

description.narrative:
The core focus of activities during the 2026–2027 biennium is to support the implementation of the Roadmap for the Elimination of Child Labour 2025–2045. Priority actions will strengthen national and subnational stakeholders’ capacity to systematically use National Labour Force Survey (SAKERNAS) data as a primary reference for the design and implementation of national programmes. At the same time, activities will initiate a critical review and updating of the list of hazardous occupations for children, taking into account technological change and digital disruption. Where feasible, this process will also seek to encourage regulatory revisions to ensure continued relevance and effectiveness. In parallel, efforts will reinforce child labour elimination in key sectors, particularly plantations, fisheries, and critical minerals, where risks remain acute.
In the context of eliminating trafficking in persons and forced labour, a comprehensive revitalization of existing programmes is required. Planned interventions will encourage stakeholders to adopt more contextualized and responsive approaches to emerging developments, including platform work, global supply chains, and forced labour import bans, while strengthening operational mechanisms for mandate implementation, coordination, and programme evaluation. Establishing clear and permanent inter-ministerial coordination arrangements, alongside meaningful engagement of employers, workers, and civil society organizations, is essential to ensure that these issues are understood and addressed as structural challenges within both the world of work and broader humanitarian frameworks.
The CPO is essential in the fight against child labour and forced labour, while also promoting decent work. It encourages initiatives that foster better working conditions across supply chains in various sectors, particularly in the palm oil industry, as a strategy to prevent child labour and forced labour.
